items.text: **A v2 consideration, not v1 or v1.5: JobsPipe (https://jobspipe.dev) as an alternative to the approach above, not an addition to it.** It would remove the need for a second request and any HTML parsing, Verified 2026-09-08 against their OpenAPI spec (jobspipe.dev/openapi.json) and terms page, the `Job` schema's `description` field reads "Full text of the posting as published by the source", against Adzuna's 500 character excerpt; it also returns `seniority`, `work_arrangement` (remote/hybrid/onsite), `status` (active/closed), `keyword_slugs`, `min/max_annual_salary_usd`, and `discovered_at` for incremental polling; credits are 1 per job returned, `blur_company_data=true` returns rows for zero credits, the free tier is 1,000 jobs a month with `limit` capped at 25 (about 50 searches a month at 20 listings each, against the current cap of roughly 108), and the first paid tier is $49 a month for 25,000; their terms state no attribution requirement, which would make spec 0013's AC-6 and AC-7 apparatus (the attribution component, the logo geometry, the mandated link targets) deletable rather than portable; their terms do **not** address caching or storage, a gap rather than a permission, and this app stores listing fields on `application` rows, so that has to be resolved with the vendor in writing before anyone relies on it. Two other places already point at this same decision, so treat it as one rather than three: `docs/feature-14-v2-architecture.md`'s extract-then-score pipeline names full posting text as its own unmet precondition and is not referenced anywhere else in this scope; and spec 0016's Consequences already names the switching cost, that feature 15's sixteen ground truth pairs stop matching what the model sees the moment full postings arrive and need a deliberate re-authoring pass.

OG image alt: `JobHunt. Shows its work, not just a score. An example match of 8 out of 11 skills.` It describes what the card actually renders (the mark, the `COPY-3` headline, the match chip). If `COPY-3` ever changes, this changes with it.

**AC-9 names a pairing mechanism the code does not use, and the difference is load bearing rather than cosmetic.** AC-9 and the Value sourcing table (line 100) both say outcomes are matched back to their card "by `sourceJobId`, never the array index". `ScoredResults` in `src/app/(app)/search/page.tsx:442` pairs by array index, at the one point where `scoreListings()` guarantees one outcome per listing in order, and then carries that pair through the reorder so nothing later matches on a position that has since changed. **The guarantee AC-9 exists to protect does hold**, and as of 2026-09-07 it is proven rather than assumed by `src/app/(app)/search/page.test.ts`'s pairing test, which was shown to fail when a row takes its listing from the sorted array and its outcome from the unsorted one, a break both neighbouring ordering tests pass. The difference that matters: index pairing is safe only while `scoreListings()` keeps returning one outcome per listing in order, where a `sourceJobId` keyed pairing would not depend on that guarantee at all. So this is a real choice, not just wording: correct the spec to describe index pairing before the sort, or decide the `sourceJobId` keyed pairing is genuinely wanted and change the code to match. **That choice belongs to `/architect`**, and this entry deliberately does not make it.
**`COPY-3`, the OG image headline** (**AC-11**), the line set in Space Grotesk on the preview card. It may differ from the page's h1. `Shows its work, not just a score.`

**AC-9's stated assumption, made explicit and falsifiable**: because `checkFitScore()` for a listing is only ever called after that listing's own `scoreListing()` succeeds (AC-5), and `usage_cap`'s seeded ceilings are identical for `ai_scoring` and `ai_check` at every cadence (spec 0012 AC-8), the check tier's budget cannot be exhausted while the scoring tier's own budget still has room, PROVIDED every `ai_check` call in production is one this feature dispatches. Four named ways this can break, any one of which is reason to revisit AC-9: (1) this feature's sample rate is ever lowered below 1.0; (2) `usage_cap`'s two tiers are ever set to different ceilings; (3) a batch straddles a `usage_cap` window boundary (the daily and monthly caps reset on a UTC clock), since a listing scored just before the boundary can be checked just after it, spending against the new window's `ai_check` cap while the matching `ai_scoring` spend landed in the window that just closed, breaking the same window assumption even though the per listing ordering (score, then check) never does; (4) any future caller dispatches an `ai_check` call outside this feature's own scored-then-checked chain (a live test, a future eval of the check itself), which would consume budget this invariant does not account for.
Score a listing against the profile and stated preferences, and show the work: the skills that matched and the skills that are missing, not just a number.

**AC-6**: Every printed and reported verdict names its own denominator (e.g. "good_match, 3 of 3 succeeded" or, for a distribution shaped verdict, "3 strong_match / 2 possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), never just a band on its own,

items.text: A public page at `/demo` showing a fixed, already scored set of fake job listings under two example candidate profiles, so a visitor can see the product's ranking output without signing up and without the app spending a real search or scoring call.

The replacement keeps the same public, no sign in `/demo` page but scores real Adzuna listings for real, under two fictional candidate profiles that are now the only fabricated element and are shown on the page as the whole disclosure. Rows come from a manually triggered refresh (two opposed Adzuna searches, revised 2026-09-15, `"backend engineer"` and `"frontend engineer"`, one per candidate's own first desired title, up to four listings kept from each by an alternating walk, every kept listing scored for real against each persona, written to the demo table), not a build time migration, so the result set is periodically real rather than hand picked. A richer version (a real seeded account with applications and a dashboard) is a separate, still deferred idea; see Deferred below.

**AC-5**: The score schema exposes `matchedSkills` (the caller's own skills whose name, or a clear synonym, appears in the listing's visible title or description) and `notMentionedSkills` (skills from the caller's own list that a role like this one would typically value, that do not appear anywhere in the listing's visible text). Both arrays are filtered after parsing to names that case insensitively match one of the caller's own `profile_skill` names; any other name the model returns is dropped before it reaches the UI, never displayed and never a reason to fail the whole call. Neither the schema field name nor any displayed label ever reads "missing skills"; the UI's label for `notMentionedSkills` states plainly that this is not a confirmed absence (`COPY-2`).

**AC-9**: The result list renders immediately, in Adzuna's original order, with a pending indicator on every card while scoring runs in the background. It re-sorts exactly once, once every listing's outcome (a score, a gate refusal, or a failure) has resolved: scored cards first, ordered by band (`strong_match` first, `not_a_match` last, ties within a band keeping Adzuna's original relative order,), then every refused or failed card after them in its own original relative order. No further re-sort happens after that. Outcomes are matched back to their card by `sourceJobId` (never by array position),

No table stores a band or a fit score, verified by searching every file in `supabase/migrations/` for `band` and `fit_score` and finding no match, so there is nothing to migrate and no stored score to become inconsistent.

**AC-19** (new 2026-09-14): A real employer's name and a real listing's content render exactly as returned, whatever band either persona receives, including `weak_match` and `not_a_match`. Nothing on the page is hidden, blurred, or altered based on a score.

**Also the natural owner of a retention rule** (fresh model review, 2026-09-03): rows accumulate one per account per week plus two per day plus two per month, indefinitely, with no pruning and the only removal path an unbuilt feature 31's account deletion cascade. This is now a privacy question, not just a storage one, since `usage_gate_counter` is listed under "Your job search usage" in the privacy notice (`src/features/legal/stored-fields.ts`) with no stated retention period for what it keeps forever.

**AC-6**: Every rendered result carries its own "Jobs by Adzuna" attribution, at least 116 by 23 pixels, through `Card.Footer`'s `attribution` slot (spec 0005, AC-10): the word "Jobs" links to `https://www.adzuna.com`, and the word "Adzuna" is the Adzuna logo image, also linked to `https://www.adzuna.com`.

**AC-7**: A result whose salary is predicted (Adzuna's `salary_is_predicted: true`) shows "(estimated)" beside the figure and carries the separate Jobsworth attribution: a 20 by 20 pixel icon plus the words "Adzuna Jobsworth", both linked to `http://www.adzuna.co.uk/jobs/salary-predictor.html`, with the mouseover text "Salary estimate powered by Adzuna Jobsworth". A stated, non predicted salary shows neither the label nor the Jobsworth attribution.
Eval ground truth set

**Fetch the full job posting for scoring and tailoring**: fetch `job_url`'s full text instead of working from Adzuna's 500 character snippet. Two consumers now, not one: scoring (feature 14) and, the stronger case, generating a tailored resume in feature 25,

**First hard measurement, 2026-09-15.** A real refresh scored 8 real Adzuna listings against two candidate profiles, and **6 of the 8 own role rows came back with zero matched skills at all**, on postings whose titles match the candidate's own first desired title. The cause is the 500 character excerpt Adzuna returns, which usually carries company boilerplate rather than requirements. That result fired spec 0021's own pre-registered stopping rule, which concluded the snippet is the cause and froze the two demo queries rather than re-tuning them, so the measurement closes a question instead of opening one.

**AC-11**: `src/app/opengraph-image.tsx` produces a 1200 by 630 pixel PNG at build time, showing the JobHunt mark, the page headline, and the match chip, drawn on the brand token values, and exports `alt`, `size` and `contentType`.

**AC-8**: `usage_cap` holds six seed rows from this feature's migration: `(ai_scoring, account, week, 500)`, `(ai_scoring, global, day, 1320)`, `(ai_scoring, global, month, 40000)`, `(ai_check, account, week, 500)`, `(ai_check, global, day, 1320)`, `(ai_check, global, month, 40000)`. These are `job_search`'s own cadence numbers (25 / 66 / 2000 searches) multiplied by `RESULTS_PER_PAGE` (`src/features/search/adzuna.ts:36`, `= 20`); `ai_check` mirrors `ai_scoring` at its own sample rate of 1.0. Neither tier is `usage_gate_misconfigured` from the moment this feature ships.
**AC-5**: A listing's check runs only after that listing's own `scoreListing()` call resolves with `{ allowed: true }`. A refused or failed score never triggers a check call.

**AC-9**: An `ai_check` gate refusal adds no page level notice of its own (unlike spec 0015 AC-11's scoring refusal notice); it renders only through AC-7's unverifiable state. This rests on an explicit, falsifiable assumption, stated in this spec's Key invariants: because a check only ever follows a successful score, and both tiers share identical `usage_cap` ceilings (spec 0012 AC-8), `ai_check`'s budget cannot exhaust before `ai_scoring`'s already has, by which point spec 0015 AC-11's own notice is already showing.

Export `resolvedModel()` from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts`, and add `bandAnchorsHash()` as a small pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`. Write the pure verdict logic in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`: the three way outcome classification (refusal, rerun failure, scored success) from AC-3, the majority vote with the 3 of 5 inconclusive floor and the no majority/`acceptableBands` exception, the distinct `stability-probe` "every success inside `acceptableBands`" rule (AC-4), and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison (AC-5). Wire `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts` against constructed fixtures for each rule, no vendor call involved. Satisfies **AC-3**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**.

Happy path: `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` scores that one pair for real, five sequential reruns under the one minted session, and prints a passing verdict with its denominator (e.g. "strong_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), verifies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-6**, **AC-9**.

Verdict logic: the pure rerun outcome classification, majority vote with its no majority and `acceptableBands` exception, the `stability-probe` rule, and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison, each proved against constructed fixtures with no vendor call, satisfies AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6.

**AC-13**: `Listing` refuses an empty or whitespace only `sourceJobId`, `title` or `companyName`. Such an item is dropped by feature 11's existing per item parse as an ordinary bad row, so it never reaches the results list and never reaches an insert that the table's check constraints would refuse.
**AC-15**: `salary_is_predicted` is declared in `STORED_FIELDS` with a plain words description,

**AC-6**: `application.salary_is_predicted` exists as a nullable boolean, and a check constraint makes it present exactly when `salary_min` or `salary_max` is present. When Adzuna stated no pay at all, the column is written `null` and never `false`,

**AC-7**: An application row whose stored salary was predicted renders `(estimated)` beside the figure and carries the Jobsworth attribution, matching spec 0013's AC-7 exactly: a 20 by 20 pixel icon plus the words `Adzuna Jobsworth`, both linked to `ADZUNA_JOBSWORTH_URL`, with the mouseover text `Salary estimate powered by Adzuna Jobsworth`. A stored non predicted salary renders neither.

**AC-8**: Every application row displayed on `/applications` carries its own `Jobs by Adzuna` attribution through `Card.Footer`'s attribution slot, on the same terms spec 0013 AC-6 sets for a search result, with the link target read from `ADZUNA_ATTRIBUTION_URL`. Attribution renders once per displayed row and never once per screen (spec 0013, invariant 4). A page with no rows shows no attribution block.

Write `src/features/scoring/rubric.ts`: the five band anchors (their exact wording), the Zod `fitScoreSchema` (`band` enum, `matchedSkills`, `notMentionedSkills`, `reasoning` capped at 600 characters, the three value `sponsorshipSignal` enum), the post-parse skill name filter, and the prompt builder taking a bounded profile and one listing, including the truncation caveat, the missing-description case, and the untrusted input instructions. Satisfies **AC-1**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**, **AC-12**, **AC-13**, and is the anchor wording **AC-2** is later measured against.

Write `src/features/scoring/score-card.tsx`: the band badge, the matched and not mentioned lists, the reasoning, the optional sponsorship badge, plus the pending state and the per card failure state, taking a `ScoreOutcome | "pending"` prop so it renders every state this feature has from day one. Satisfies the display half of **AC-5**, **AC-6**.

**AC-3**: The check's schema output, `ungroundedSkills`, is filtered after parsing to only names present in the `matchedSkills` list sent to it, using the same normalization `normalizeFitScore()` already applies to `matchedSkills` itself (case, whitespace, canonicalised to the caller's own spelling), so a name that only differs in case or formatting is matched rather than dropped as invented. This mirrors spec 0015 AC-5's own filter and reuses its normalization rather than a second, independently written one.

Rubric, schema and prompt: the five band anchors, `fitScoreSchema`, the post-parse skill name filter, and the prompt builder handling the 500 character truncation caveat and a missing description (AC-1, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6, AC-12, AC-13, the anchor wording AC-2 is later measured against)

Widen the thread from one listing to all 20: swap the single `scoreListing()` call from step 4 for `scoreListings()` inside the same Suspense boundary, whose fallback now renders the whole list unscored, in Adzuna's original order, with every card in its pending state (the Strategic Suspense Boundaries pattern named in Decision). Satisfies **AC-9**'s immediate render half.

Add the resolved states: sort the outcomes by band once all have resolved (**AC-9**'s re-sort half), the per card failure state (**AC-10**), and the page level cap reached notice reusing `SENTENCES` (**AC-11**).
No check outcome ever moves a listing between bands or changes the batch's sort order (AC-12); the one time re-sort (spec 0015 AC-9) is complete before any check outcome is known to exist.

**AC-12**: No check outcome ever changes a listing's displayed band. Band selection and the one time re-sort (spec 0015 AC-9) are computed before any check outcome exists and are never revisited by one.

Concurrent dispatch and ranking: `scoreListings()`, widening the Suspense boundary to all 20 listings, the one time sort by band, the per card failure state, and the page level cap reached notice (AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, AC-11, AC-14, AC-16)

Update the demo card component: add the compact other persona band line (AC-16), the ungrounded skills rendering (removed from the matched list, `SCORING_COPY.removedSkills(...)` and `.reasoningCaveat` reused verbatim), render `AdzunaAttribution` unconditionally and the `(estimated)` label plus `JobsworthAttribution` together when `salary_is_predicted` (AC-9), and make the not mentioned skills caption conditional on the snippet actually being truncated. Satisfies **AC-8**, **AC-9**, **AC-16**, **AC-19**.

A real employer's name now appears on a public portfolio page next to a `weak_match` or `not_a_match` band (AC-19), an editorial exposure spec 0021's fabricated version never carried and Adzuna's terms do not govern either way.
Honesty: a listing whose band is `weak_match` or `not_a_match` still renders its real employer name, unhidden. Verifies **AC-19**.

The opposite is now true on purpose: every listing (company name, title, description, location) is real, exactly as Adzuna returned it, including a real employer's name on a `weak_match` or `not_a_match` row (AC-19). The two candidate personas are the only fictional element left, and they are shown on the page in full (AC-14) as the disclosure that makes this honest.

Read path and rendering: both personas read in one pass, the cross persona band line, ungrounded skill rendering, real Adzuna/Jobsworth attribution, and the wording pass removing every claim that the page is fabricated, satisfies AC-1, AC-7, AC-10 through AC-16, AC-19
a named real employer's posting always shows its real name and content whatever band it receives, including `weak_match` and `not_a_match` (spec 0021 AC-19);

The asset is `src/features/search/adzuna-logo.svg`, rendered inline from `adzuna-logo-geometry.ts`. Both the word and the mark link to `https://www.adzuna.com`, verified against Adzuna's own terms of service and recorded in spec 0013 AC-6. The row at line 86 below guessed those targets and guessed wrong; it has been corrected in the same pass.

**AC-10**: The `Card` component's footer slot accepts an optional `attribution` node beside the primary action link, laid out `justify-between` and wrapping to a stacked layout before a 116 by 23 pixel block would otherwise compress. This feature builds and tests the slot mechanism only; the real Adzuna attribution content is built in feature 11 (see `## Follow-up`).

Thicken: the `AdzunaAttribution` component (the real logo asset once sourced, both link targets) placed in `Card.Footer`'s `attribution` slot, and the Jobsworth badge (icon, text, link, mouseover) shown beside a predicted salary, plus the "(estimated)" label. Satisfies **AC-6**, **AC-7**, **AC-8**.
Happy path: a signed in user with a `job_preference` row searches with a real title, sees real Adzuna listings with working attribution and outbound links, verifies **AC-1**, **AC-6**, **AC-8**.
Predicted salary: a listing carrying `salary_is_predicted: true` renders the estimate label and the Jobsworth attribution; one carrying `false` (or no salary) renders neither, verifies **AC-7**.

**Done 2026-09-13**: a sweep of all of `docs/` for numeric references into that file found exactly four, all re read against the file on 2026-09-13: this spec's `index.md:110`, the `hasQuery` conditional, 94 to **129**; this spec's `rationale.md:111`, the `Promise.all` over the applied and scoring reads inside `SearchOutcome`, 243 to **291**; and spec 0015's `index.md:211` and `verify.md:78`, both citing the `ScoredResults` index pairing (`const paired = listings.map(...)`), 383 to **442** in each. Corrected in the same pass rather than one at a time.

The `weak_match` and `not_a_match` boundary is still undefined and is still recorded as a gap in spec [0016](../0016-eval-ground-truth-set/index.md)'s Follow up. **Three pairs sit on it, not two**, across thirty reruns: `key-domain-mismatch` (3 to 2, then 0 to 5), `weak-match-shallow-overlap` (4 to 1, then 3 to 2) and `boundary-seniority-gap` (`weak_match` 4 of 5 both runs, passing only through its widened tolerance). The one to watch is `weak-match-shallow-overlap`: it carries no tolerance and at 3 to 2 is a single rerun away from having no majority at all, so it is the pair most likely to fail next and the failure would be the boundary, not the pair. What would justify acting is repeated flipping, not one split.

**Should `control-one-gap` keep its `control` tag?** This pair no longer behaves that way: `possible_match` won it 4 to 1, then 5 to 0, then 3 to 2 on the confirming run, so it now passes on the narrowest majority the harness accepts. Spec [0016](../0016-eval-ground-truth-set/index.md) draws this exact distinction when it explains why `mild-stretch-possible-match` carries "no `acceptableBands` and the plain `control` tag rather than `boundary`": the tag tracks whether the anchor text settles the pair, not how the model happens to answer. **Recorded here, not answered.** Whoever takes it up should know the two obvious moves are both constrained: retagging it `boundary` would concede that the anchors do not settle it, which contradicts this spec's own finding that they do, and widening it with `acceptableBands` is refused outright by the Key invariants above. `ground-truth.test.ts` now asserts that no `control` tagged pair carries `acceptableBands`, so the retag and the tolerance are not independent choices.

**AC-4b**: Spec 0016's two now stale references to `control-one-gap` are corrected: its table row at line 141 lists the pair as `good_match`, and its Follow up at line 182 quotes that pair's rationale saying "That is good_match's wording" as present tense evidence of how the set was authored. The row is updated and the Follow up quote is marked as historical, true of the set as authored and superseded here. Both are recording edits, not changes to what spec 0016 decides.

Full attribution and states: the real "Jobs by Adzuna" and Jobsworth attribution, the estimated salary label, the `job_preference` prefill, and the three distinct visible states (AC-4, AC-6, AC-7, AC-9) · done 2026-09-04.

**The thin thread.** Commit `assets/SpaceGrotesk-SemiBold.ttf` beside its licence file after confirming the licence permits it; build `src/app/opengraph-image.tsx` with its `alt`, `size` and `contentType` exports, drawing the mark inline as SVG rectangles; set the page's title, description and `metadataBase` from `canonicalSiteUrl`; and stand up `EntryHeader`, a bare hero `Section`, and `EntryFooter`. Deploy to a Vercel preview and confirm in a real client that the card unfurls. Satisfies **AC-10**, **AC-11**, **AC-12**, **AC-13**, **AC-15**. The footer's copyright is `COPY-4` and the image headline is `COPY-3`, so both must be written before this step runs.
`manual` Link card: the deployed preview URL unfurls with a real 1200 by 630 image, a title and a description, in at least two clients, verifies **AC-10**, **AC-11**.

The thin thread: the `Logo` base component, the committed Space Grotesk file and its licence, the generated `opengraph-image.tsx`, page title and description off `canonicalSiteUrl`, a header and footer shell, then a real preview deployment whose link card is confirmed to unfurl, plus the token drift guard, satisfies AC-1, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13, AC-15, AC-16

Write the migration seeding the six `usage_cap` rows for `ai_scoring` and `ai_check` at the corrected values (`500` / `1320` / `40000`, see Rationale). Blocked until feature 10's `usage_cap` table exists on `main` (see Consequences), satisfies **AC-8**.

Write the critical test scenarios above: the `classify()` unit tests (no vendor call needed), a zeroed cap refusing without reaching a vendor, and, gated behind `TEST_LIVE_MODEL_CALLS_ENABLED`, both tiers reaching two real, different vendors, satisfies **AC-1** through **AC-8**.

Failure case: a `usage_cap` row set to `0` for a tier in a test refuses every call to that tier with `success({ allowed: false, reason: "account_week_cap_reached" })` (or the matching reason), and the vendor is never called, verifies **AC-4**, **AC-8**.

**AC-11**: When any of the concurrent calls is refused by the usage gate (`{ allowed: false }`), the affected cards show no band and no per card failure note. Instead, one page level notice appears once, naming the limit reached (reusing the existing `SENTENCES` table keyed by `UsageGateReason`, spec 0011). When refusals in the same batch carry more than one distinct reason, the notice uses whichever reason the first refused call, in the listing's original order, carried. Kept visibly distinct from the per card failure state in AC-10.

Extend `score-listings.ts`: change `scoreListings()`'s per listing dispatch to, after `scoreListing()` resolves, call `checkFitScore()` (threading the same `cookieAdapter` seam) when the score succeeded and `matchedSkills` is non-empty (AC-4, AC-5), otherwise record the matching skip variant; change the return type to `readonly ListingOutcome[]`; extend the existing `scoring.score_listings` span with the four new attributes once every outcome resolves, satisfies **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-10**.

Update `score-listings.test.ts` and `src/app/(app)/search/page.test.ts` for the new `ListingOutcome` return shape (spec 0015's own scoring assertions are unaffected; `scoreListing()` itself is untouched), and write this feature's own critical test scenarios above, satisfies **AC-1** through **AC-13**.

Failure case, unverifiable: a constructed `ai_check` vendor error and a zeroed `ai_check` `usage_cap` row both resolve to the AC-7 unverifiable state on the affected card, with the displayed matched skills unchanged, verifies **AC-7**, **AC-9**.

If a future change ever lowers the check tier's sample rate below 1.0, gives `ai_scoring` and `ai_check` different `usage_cap` ceilings, or adds any `ai_check` caller outside this feature's own scored-then-checked chain, AC-9's decision to skip a page level notice for a check refusal must be revisited; the four named ways this can break are stated in Key invariants specifically so they can be checked again, including the UTC window boundary case.

**AC-7**: Once a listing's score and, when applicable, its check have both resolved, the card renders exactly one of three states: clean (nothing to note), flagged (each ungrounded skill removed from the displayed matched list, with one note naming the removed skill or skills, stating they could not be verified against the excerpt shown), or unverifiable (a note that skill matches could not be checked for this listing, with the displayed matched list left exactly as scored). Unverifiable covers a check timeout, a vendor error, and a gate refusal alike, rendered identically at the card level, even though a refusal and a failure remain two structurally distinct results (spec 0012's own invariant, unchanged).

Configuration: `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google` and `ai` added, the two vendor keys validated in `src/env.ts`, and the six `usage_cap` seed rows migrated for `ai_scoring` and `ai_check` (AC-8, AC-10)
Tests: the source guard, the `classify()` unit tests, and the gated real vendor integration tests (AC-1 through AC-8)

Wire the check into `scoreListings()`'s dispatch and into `page.tsx` / `score-card.tsx`'s rendering (the three card states, the reasoning caveat, the unchanged band), covers AC-4, AC-5, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, AC-12, AC-13.

Observability and tests: extend the `scoring.score_listings` span, update the existing test suites for the new `ListingOutcome` shape, and write this feature's own critical test scenarios, covers AC-1 through AC-13.
(see Rationale)

**AC-1**: One command (`pnpm eval`) runs every pair in feature 15's committed set and prints, for each pair, a pass, fail, or inconclusive verdict together with the actual band(s) observed. Before minting any session or spending any vendor call, a top level `beforeAll` runs `validateGroundTruth()` against the committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS`; if it returns any issue, the run throws with every issue printed, one per line, and exits non zero. This check runs even under a `-t` filtered invocation (AC-8),

**AC-2**: Every pair is scored through the real `scoreListing()` path, passing the run's one minted fixture session (`session.jar`) as its `cookieAdapter` argument, exactly the shape `test/integration/fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already uses. One session is minted once for the whole run (not once per pair), reused by every call. A pair's five reruns happen one after another inside that pair's own test body (never fired at once), because they exist to measure how much the same input moves between separate calls; different pairs' test bodies may run at the same time as each other, bounded by an explicit concurrency limit (Build plan, step 1).
**AC-3**: `scoreListing()` can return three kinds of outcome, and each is handled differently:

**AC-4**: A pair tagged `stability-probe` is judged differently, but only once AC-3's own 3 of 5 successes floor is met (fewer than 3 successes is still `inconclusive` under AC-3, unchanged). With 3 or more successes, `expectedBand` is not consulted and no majority is computed: the pair passes only if every one of its successful reruns' band is inside `acceptableBands`. One success landing outside that set fails the pair even if every other success matched, since this pair's whole point is that no single run should be trusted as the answer. Because there may be no single winning band, this pair's verdict is always reported as its observed distribution (e.g. `{ strong_match: 3, possible_match: 2 }`), never a lone band.

**AC-5**: The three `preference-isolation` tagged pairs (`preference-match`, `preference-violation`, `preference-title-conflict`) are each judged individually by AC-3 first, exactly like any other pair, with no special treatment of their own verdicts. Once all three have a verdict that is neither `inconclusive` nor missing (skipped by a `-t` filter that excluded one of them, in which case the check below is skipped and reported as `leak-check-skipped`), the run additionally compares `preference-match`'s verdict band against `preference-violation`'s and against `preference-title-conflict`'s:

**AC-9**: The command writes a JSON report every run, in addition to the console table, to a directory this repository does not track, at `test/eval/.output/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced by dashes>.json`, creating that directory if it does not exist. Each report is a single `EvalReport` object (defined in `test/eval/report.ts`) recording: the filter used (if any) and every skipped pair id; per pair, its status (`pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`), sub reason where relevant, denominator, and every observed band (or band distribution); the preference leak check's own outcome; the run's overall status and aborted reason if any; and, once per report, which model answered (via the shared `resolvedModel()` guard on `TIERS.ai_scoring.model`, never a name typed into the harness) and a hash of `BAND_ANCHORS`'s current text (`bandAnchorsHash()`, defined once and shared with the AC-10 test, so "the same way" is true by construction rather than by two separate implementations agreeing).
